newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND UPSTAGE SRI LANKA IN CHAMPIONS TROPHY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND UPSTAGE SRI LANKA IN CHAMPIONS TROPHY.

text.p: New Zealand, fired by a disciplined performance from their frontline bowlers, upstaged world champions Sri Lanka by 29 runs in the opening match of the Singer Champions' Trophy tournament on Thursday.

Defending a modest total of 206 on a good batting strip, New Zealand's bowling attack, backed up by crisp fielding, did not allow Sri Lanka's normally flamboyant batsmen any room to execute their shots.

Aravinda de Silva offered some resistance together with Hashan Tillakaratne, but they were unable to dominate the New Zealand attack, who struck at regular intervals to dismiss their rivals for 177 in 49.1 overs.
De Silva scored a sedate 47 off 74 balls before falling to a lazy shot while Tillakaratne made 41 off 78 balls.
Sri Lanka lost the way the moment New Zealand eliminated both the openers -- Sanath Jayasuriya and Romesh Kaluwitharana -- with 40 runs on the board.
Requiring 71 runs in the last 10 overs with five wickets in hand, Danny Morrison and Chris Cairns, returning for their second spells, struck quickly to end Sri Lanka's hopes.
Cairns, followed his innings of 71, with two for 39 while Morrison, Simon Doull and Chris Harris also bowled economically for their respective two-wicket hauls.
Coach Steve Rixon attributed his first victory in his first match with the side to "team spirit".
"Despite a small total to defend, the boys showed a great determination and confidence in their abilities," he said.
Sri Lankan manager Duleep Mendis said: "We batted poorly and paid the price. But then this is just the beginning of the tournament. We will come back and, hopefully, win the tournament."
